body:
The PathPilot mill tool-table export format, from a real 770MX export (PathPilot, 2026-11-18). The file has 1002 lines: two header rows and one row per tool number 1-1000.

Row 1 (a marker PathPilot needs on import):
```
Mill Tool Table,<date and time> - v1,This must be the first row - do not edit
```
Row 2 (column names):
```
Tool number,Description,Z offset,Diameter,Z offset wear,Diameter wear,Max RPM
```
Rows 3+ (empty tools have an empty description and zeros):
```
1,endmill [1/8] 2FL R:0.000 loc:0.375 carbide dia:0.125 [37368],1.0000000,0.1250000,0.0000000,0.0000000,0.0
8,Slitting Saw [1/8] 30FL R:0.000 uncoated carbide dia:3.000 [34993],5.0000000,3.0000000,0.0000000,0.0000000,0.0
10,drill dia:0.500,2.0000000,0.5000000,0.0000000,0.0000000,0.0
99,,3.0000000,0.0000000,0.0000000,0.0000000,-2.0
```

Notes for the parser and the writer:
- Units are the machine's (inch here). Values have 7 decimals.
- The type, flutes, corner radius `R:`, length of cut `loc:`, material and Tormach part number `[nnnnn]` live only in the free-text Description (the PathPilot tool-description format). An import reads them from there when present and keeps the text as the tool's name.
- `Z offset` is the tool length offset; on many machines it is a placeholder until measured, so the import must not treat it as a stick-out.
- The probe (T99 here) has no description and a `Max RPM` of -2.0; a negative Max RPM is a marker, not a speed.
- A file from PathPilot's Import must keep row 1 exactly as shown.

Scope widened: the same import/export now also covers **Hurco WinMax** tool libraries, so both controllers share one design (one importer with a reader per controller format, one exporter with a writer per format).

Sample: vilts attached a real export from a Hurco VMX30U, WinMax 09.01.393.30, on #2573: `atc_mtc.zip` -> `atc_mtc.TCM`.

## Hurco `.TCM` format, as read from that sample

- UTF-8 XML with a BOM, CRLF line ends. Root `<Hurco_Document Version="1.1">`, a `<FileInfo>` block (language, save date and user, machine `VMX30U`, `SoftwareVersion 09.01.393.30`), then `<Tools>`.
- 119 `<Tool Id="<guid>">` entries. Fields seen (count of tools that have it): `Name` (119), `Number` (119), `Diameter` (119), `ThreadDiameter`, `ToolLength` (119), `ShankDiameter`, `FluteLength` (117), `AbsoluteGaugeLength` (117, the measured gauge length), `ImportZeroCal`, `ToolType` (115, a number), `NumberOfFlutes` (33), `ThreadPitch` (16), `Angle` (11), `TipRadius` (6), `InnerDiameter`, `ThreadName`, `TipDiameter`, `Manufacturer`, per-material `SpeedFeeds`, plus control state (`UsedTime`, `Flags`, `GeometryFlags`, probe offset indexes).
- Units are millimetres in this file (a machine set to inch may differ - to check).
- `ToolType` is a number; the sample pairs them with names: 1 CENTER DRILL, 2 CHAMFER MILL, 3 CORNER ROUND MILL, 7 ENGRAVING MILL, 8 KEYSEAT MILL, 11 DRILL, 14 FLAT END MILL, 17 BACK SPOTFACE, 18 PROBE, 22 MULTI CUTTER THREAD MILL, 26 SINGLE CUTTER THREAD MILL (others: 6, 9, 12, 15, 16 - to map from Hurco's public WinMax tool documentation).

## Notes for the Hurco reader and writer

- Map `ToolType` to CamCraft kinds; a type CamCraft has no kind for is refused by name, not guessed.
- `AbsoluteGaugeLength` is a measured length (unlike PathPilot's placeholder Z offsets): use it for the holder gauge length.
- Keep the Hurco control fields (`UsedTime`, `Flags`, offsets) untouched on a round trip: the export writes back only what CamCraft owns, so importing CamCraft's file into WinMax does not reset tool life or probe data. Whether WinMax accepts a partial file, or needs every field, is a question for the owner's control.
- Clean-room: the format is read from the user's own file and Hurco's public docs only.

Done means (added): the Hurco sample reads into tools with the right numbers, kinds, diameters and gauge lengths (a test with the recorded `.TCM`); an exported `.TCM` that WinMax 9.01 imports (checked once on the owner's control).

Escalated from effort:medium to effort:high under the work-issue scope rule.

The latest scope includes PathPilot CSV and Hurco TCM import and export.
It also requires an undoable import, MCP support, and preservation of Hurco control fields.
This is new behavior with new tests, rather than one module that follows a known pattern.
The issue still has open questions about Hurco units, tool kinds, and acceptance of exported files.

No claim was made. No branch, worktree, code change, or test was created.
No held work exists. The issue remains open for a worker with the higher effort level.
